 Julia Gomez USA TODAY Nov. 20, 2026, 1:05 p.m. ET Hear this story A company is recalling thousands of units of toothpaste and mouthwash made for kids and adults due to cross-contamination, according to the Food and Drug Administration (FDA).
 The voluntary recall comes after the FDA notified ORL Labs that testing found hormones in samples of its ORL Organic Oral Care products, according to an FDA's enforcement report . ORL Labs did not respond to USA TODAY's request for comment on the recall.
 The recall was originally initiated on Oct. 12 but was classified as a Class II recall earlier this month. A Class II classification means the product could "cause temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences," according to the FDA .
 The recall includes 51,762 units of six different types of toothpaste and mouthwash made for both adults and children, and distributed nationwide.
 Here's what to know about the recall.

See affected models Breakfast sandwiches sold to employee break rooms, cafes recalled Why are the toothpaste and mouthwash products being recalled?
 Samples of the products "found the presence of progesterone, estradiol, or dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA)," the FDA recall report stated. It did not specify how much or which of the hormones were found in the samples.
 The FDA does not state how cross-contamination could have occurred.
 What should you do if you bought the recalled toothpaste and mouthwast products?
 The FDA report does not state what people should do if they purchased the recalled products.
 Anyone with questions can contact ORL Lab by phone at 844-675-5227 or by email at orl@orlcares.com.
